sections.content:
You know absolute superlatives in *-ísimo* from B1 Unit 7 (*utilísimo*) and evaluative *resultar* + adjective from B1 Unit 15 (*El argumento resulta convincente*). Putting them together—alongside vivid attitude adjectives—gives your spoken and written evaluations real punch.

*Resultar* ("to come across as, to turn out to be") frames a considered reaction: *La plaza resulta entrañable* ("The square comes across as endearing"), *Ese discurso resultó cursi* ("That speech came across as cheesy"), *La espera resultó agotadora*. Add *-ísimo/-ísima/-ísimos/-ísimas* to raise the intensity: *El mercado resulta animadísimo los sábados*.

Watch spelling changes before *-ísimo*: *-co → -quísimo* (*rico → riquísimo*), *-go → -guísimo* (*largo → larguísimo*), and *-z → -císimo* (*feliz → felicísimo*). Never stack *muy* before *-ísimo* (*muy riquísimo* ✗) and keep gender/number agreement with the subject of *resultar*.

sections.title: Spelling changes in -ísimo and pairing with resultar
rows: *El pan de esa esquina resulta riquísimo.*
*El tono despectivo resulta espantoso en una crónica.*

items.spanish: El barrio viejo resulta entrañable incluso en los días de lluvia.
items.english: The old neighbourhood comes across as endearing even on rainy days.

items.spanish: La despedida resultó un poco cursi, pero la cena estuvo estupenda.
items.english: The farewell came across as a bit cheesy, but dinner was terrific.

items.spanish: El mercado resulta animadísimo desde primera hora de la mañana.
items.english: The market comes across as extremely lively from first thing in the morning.

items.spanish: Ese comentario despectivo me resultó espantoso y fuera de lugar.
items.english: That dismissive remark struck me as dreadful and out of place.

sections.content: Never combine *muy* with *-ísimo* (*muy animadísimo* ✗ → *animadísimo* ✓). And remember that the adjective after *resultar* must agree in gender and number with the subject (*las filas resultaron larguísimas*).
